title: Digital Memory, Forgetting, Stigma & Restorative Passage — Archive Ethics Atlas
status: comparative digital-memory / legal / ethical / project synthesis
purpose: Give the archive a serious theory of persistence, forgetting, expiration, rehabilitation, correction reach, collective memory and restorative passage so 'archive everything' does not silently become 'freeze every person forever'.
epistemic_rule: Legal rights, platform practices, psychological effects and Potatoverse symbolism remain distinct. The right to be forgotten is jurisdiction-specific and not a universal command to erase public history. Archive ethics must balance accuracy, public interest, accountability, privacy, rehabilitation and temporal relevance.
central_epiphany: Digital archives reverse the old scarcity of memory. The problem is no longer only how to preserve the past, but how to stop preserved information from impersonating the present.

memory_layers.event_memory: what happened at a particular time
memory_layers.institutional_memory: records maintained by organizations, courts, archives or platforms
memory_layers.search_memory: what retrieval systems surface first when a name/topic is queried
memory_layers.collective_memory: shared representations of the past maintained across a community
memory_layers.self_memory: the subject's own account of continuity/change
memory_layers.project_rule: Never let one layer stand in for all the others.

digital_collective_memory.research_context: Recent digital-memory scholarship distinguishes digitized collective memory from collective memory transformed by digital platforms, trace data and algorithmic curation.
digital_collective_memory.archive_effect: The digital archive is dynamic: old material is continuously reordered through search, links, sharing and platform design rather than simply sitting inert in storage.
digital_collective_memory.project_translation: Archive is not passive memory. Retrieval architecture is part of meaning production.

memory_forgetting_dialectic.problem: Human social life historically depended on both remembering and forgetting. Digital systems lower the cost of remembering and raise the cost of social expiration.
memory_forgetting_dialectic.stainforth_relation: European digital-memory debates show tension between preservation/indexing and rights to delisting/forgetting.
memory_forgetting_dialectic.project_question: What should remain historically preserved while becoming less dominant in present identity retrieval?

right_to_be_forgotten.legal_context: European law and policy developed mechanisms for delisting certain name-linked search results under defined conditions; this does not necessarily delete the underlying publication.
right_to_be_forgotten.archive_translation: A record can remain preserved while its current discoverability, prominence or identity-binding force changes.
right_to_be_forgotten.public_interest_test: Consider role of subject, accuracy, age of information, seriousness, ongoing relevance, public interest and legal obligations.

temporal_truth.epiphany: A statement may be historically true and presently misleading at the same time.
temporal_truth.example_structure: In year t0, person occupied role/state X. At t1, circumstances changed. A search result that presents X without date/context converts historical truth into current misrepresentation.

archive_half_life.definition: How long an item continues to materially shape present attention/reputation after publication.
archive_half_life.insight: Two equally old records can have radically different social half-lives.

stigma_packet.definition: A compact label, screenshot, accusation, meme or summary that travels more easily than the full historical context.
stigma_packet.chain: complex person → compressed label → portable artifact → repeated retrieval → expectation → selective interpretation
stigma_packet.risk: Compression creates asymmetric mobility: stigma moves faster than correction because correction often requires more context.
stigma_packet.countermeasure: Attach date, evidence status, correction state, source independence and current relevance to portable summaries.

correction_asymmetry.problem: Original accusations, memes or headlines can be more emotionally salient and widely distributed than later corrections.
correction_asymmetry.archive_rule: A correction should be linked bidirectionally from the original record and surfaced in current-status views.
correction_asymmetry.ritual_relation: Correction needs its own social ceremony/status signal or it may remain informationally weaker than accusation.

historical_preservation_vs_current_ident.principle: The archive should preserve history without forcing historical roles to remain current identity labels.
implementation: avoid SEO titles that freeze obsolete states
historical_preservation_vs_current_ident.potatoverse_relation: Door is the transition operator that lets historical state remain remembered while current identity changes.

restorative_justice_online.research_context: Restorative approaches to online harm emphasize victim needs, offender accountability, understanding harm, repair and—where appropriate—reintegration rather than content removal alone.
restorative_justice_online.garden_translation: Garden asks what conditions allow damaged relations or participants to regain future capacity.
restorative_justice_online.boundary: Restorative processes are not always appropriate, safe or desired; serious abuse may require separation, legal process or protective measures.

restorative_door.definition: A socially legible passage from condemned/current role to historical/changed status when evidence supports change.
restorative_door.anti_pattern: Forgiveness without factual clarity can erase victims; permanent condemnation without transition can erase change.
restorative_door.equilibrium: remember accurately + update honestly + preserve agency

public_shaming.research_context: Recent philosophy/technology work distinguishes legitimate public accountability from wrongful or disproportionate online shaming and asks what duties platforms have in reducing the latter.
archive_tests: Is the subject a public figure or private individual?
Does circulation serve accountability or spectacle?
public_shaming.farm_relation: Public shaming becomes Farm-like when the punishment itself becomes renewable content.

collective_memory_governance.epiphany: Memory governance is power: deciding what is preserved, searchable, ranked, summarized, corrected and expired shapes collective identity.
collective_memory_governance.archive_eye: The Eye should therefore inspect not only truth/falsity but retrieval dominance, recency, context and correction state.
collective_memory_governance.ethical_target: High historical fidelity with low unnecessary identity capture.

forgetting_types.natural_forgetting: decline in social salience over time
forgetting_types.technical_expiry: automatic deletion or reduced prominence after a period
forgetting_types.legal_delisting: removal from certain name-based search results under law/policy
forgetting_types.contextual_forgetting: old material remains but is demoted behind current context
forgetting_types.forgiveness: moral/social transformation of relation without factual erasure
forgetting_types.suppression: concealment of relevant information; may be improper

archive_design_principles: Separate historical truth from current-status claims.
Make corrections as machine-readable as accusations.
Attach review/expiry metadata to sensitive identity labels.
Represent restitution and repair events as first-class graph edges.
Never use archival persistence itself as proof of present relevance.

metrics.ContextLoss: degree to which retrieved artifact lacks original setting
metrics.IdentityCaptureRisk: label dominance × archive persistence × correction asymmetry × context loss
metrics.RestorationScore: repair completion + verified change + correction visibility + role transition
